mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when RSAFS shows a sustained increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two months signals a weakening supply side, which can lead to reduced corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which boosts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over two months, it signals strong job growth, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) both increase by more than 0.5% within a month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with monetary tightening, which increases borrowing costs and erodes consumer purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) both show a decline of more than 1% over two quarters, it signals a weakening demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS decline > 1% in 2 quarters
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.
